intent: The Ken-Caryl Ranch Master Association sets a 1.75-inch minimum pile for artificial turf. Does that floor also apply to a backyard putting green, and who decides?
distinctValue: Resolves, from the association's own governing text, that the Ranch's written rules never name a putting green: the Rules, Regulations and Procedures adopted by the Architectural Committee on June 11, 2026 (45 pages) and the Fall 2023 Residential Landscaping Guidebook never use the word putting or golf; Artificial Turf Section 2.05 sets a 1.75-inch minimum pile with no carve-out; Sports Courts and Facilities Section 2.56 covers improvements such as, but not limited to, tennis courts, in-ground swimming pools and multi-purpose sports courts, so its list is not closed (the facility no more than 50% of the lot behind the front of the house, 10-foot setback, no night lighting); Play and Sports Equipment Section 2.42 requires approval for permanent installations, placed in back or shielded side yards where applicable and reviewed case by case. The same document settles who decides: an unlisted improvement still needs Committee approval, and the Committee's or Board's interpretation is final and binding. On variances it says the Committee may grant a variance to the rules if deemed appropriate, consistent with the Master Declaration; Section 1.04 quotes Master Declaration Section 8.09, which lets the Committee authorize variances from the architectural provisions of the Master Declaration or a Supplemental Declaration when circumstances such as topography, natural obstructions, hardship, or aesthetic or environmental consideration warrant, in its sole and absolute discretion, evidenced in writing and signed by at least a majority of the Committee; Section 1.02 sends variance requests to full Committee review. Nothing in it says which section reviews a putting green, whether the 1.75-inch minimum applies to one, or whether a variance reaches that Rules standard. The page therefore names the Architectural Committee and the exact questions to put to it in writing (which section reviews a putting green, does the 1.75-inch minimum apply, and if so will it consider a variance), makes no claim of its own about how short putting turf is cut, and states plainly that nothing pre-approves one. It also surfaces the collision inside the Ranch's own rulebook that no neighbouring page has: Section 2.05 requires a landscape buffer around the turf, while the Ranch's Firewise rules forbid flammable material within the first 5 feet of the foundation and juniper within 15 feet of a flammable structure — so the buffer has to be non-combustible where the lawn meets the house. And it names the actual water provider, the Ken-Caryl Ranch Water and Sanitation District, whose own outdoor rules (two days a week, a third only when needed, never more than three, nothing between 10 a.m. and 6 p.m.) differ from the assigned-day schedules on the neighbouring pages, and which voted on 22 April 2026 not to pass the Stage 1 drought surcharge to customers while telling them to keep to 2 designated days — a conflict with its own rules page that the page tells the reader to take to the district.

supports: Artificial Turf — Architectural Committee approval is required. The following rules shall apply:
Artificial turf shall only be used in backyard applications
A landscape buffer shall surround the turf area
Pile height will be a minimum of 1.75”
Color will be compatible with natural turf and be dual, tri, or quad color
Submittal shall include: 1 foot square sample of the proposed turf
Site and grading plan, showing location of installation
Landscaping plan showing the proposed layout including edging and other materials
Artificial turf may only be used in back yards. Artificial turf in side yards will be reviewed on a case-by-case basis. See also Artificial Turf Section 2.05.
Sports Courts and Facilities — Architectural Committee approval is required.
This section is related to improvements such as, but not limited to, tennis courts, in-ground swimming pools, and multi-purpose sports courts.

Location: The facility, exclusive of landscaping and screening, shall occupy no more than 50% of the surface area of that portion of the lot lying to the rear of the plane of the front of the house exclusive of the area of the house.
Setbacks: All physical improvements, including retaining walls and specialized fencing, shall be set back a minimum of 10 feet.
Lighting: Lighting of facilities for nighttime use will not be permitted.
Applications are reviewed twice a month by the Architectural Committee. Most decisions are made within two weeks, but more complex projects may take up to 30 days.
Approval is required before starting any exterior improvement
Subassociation approval may be required
For questions about properties in The Plains, contact ... For questions about properties in The Valley, contact ...

Beginning July 1, 2026, Jefferson County’s Wildfire Resiliency Code applies to permits for new construction and certain exterior improvement projects within designated Wildland-Urban Interface (WUI) areas.

The Ken-Caryl Ranch Master Association (KCRMA) encourages residents to evaluate the first 5 feet around their homes and consider replacing combustible landscaping materials with fire-hardened alternatives.

Landscaping – Architectural Committee approval is required. ... The committee seeks to achieve an aesthetically pleasing balance of planting and hardscape material within the lot. See also Artificial Turf Section 2.05.
Xeriscape Rules: Design elements such as, but not limited to, rock, engineered block, and mulch must be natural in color. For example – no red or black mulch will be permitted.
Firewise and Mitigation Efforts – Architectural Committee approval is required for all changes or additions related to Firewise and mitigation efforts.

Landscaping Near Foundations: No flammable materials, such as mulch, shall be placed within the first 5 feet of a home’s foundation. Non-flammable alternatives such as rock, gravel, or hardscape features are encouraged.
Planting Restrictions: Juniper species are not allowed within 15 feet of a flammable structure.
Vegetation Clearance: Branches on trees and bushes must be trimmed and maintained at a minimum distance of 10 feet from the home’s roof and exterior walls.

Review the project sections below to find submittal requirements, supporting documents and other information needed for your exterior improvement request. If your project is not listed, Architectural Committee approval may still be required.

NEGATIVE FINDING: pages 1-43 carry the PDF's text layer (pdftotext, layout and raw modes, and again with whitespace and hyphens collapsed), which returns zero hits for "putting", "golf" and "synthetic". Page 44 has no text layer: it is Addendum 1, a Temporary Sign Placement Map, rendered and read by eye, with no putting or golf. Page 45 is blank apart from its page number. "Green" appears as a colour (fence and garden-fence posts, play-equipment colours, trampoline pads) and inside other words: "greenhouses" and "Greenhouse" (2.01 Accessory Buildings) and "greenbelt" or "greenbelts" (inspections under enforcement, air-conditioner screening, fences, lighting, signs). "Chipping" appears only for driveways and concrete and for exterior paint. No section names, permits, prohibits or exempts a putting green, and Section 2.05 writes no exception to the 1.75-inch minimum. SCOPE: Section 2.56's list is open ("such as, but not limited to"), so the rules do not rule out a green being reviewed under it. Section 1.04 quotes Master Declaration Section 8.09, which covers variances from the architectural provisions of the Master Declaration or a Supplemental Declaration at the Committee's sole and absolute discretion; the rules do not say outright whether that reaches a Rules standard such as the 2.05 pile height, so the page puts that question to the Committee instead of stating an answer.

sources.label: Ken-Caryl Ranch Water and Sanitation District: Water Rules, Rebates, and Conservation (outdoor water use)
supports: To help conserve water and reduce water waste, the following watering rules are in effect from May 1 to October 1 each year.
There are no assigned watering days, but never water a zone more than three days a week and never between 10 a.m. and 6 p.m..
No watering between 10 a.m. and 6 p.m.
Water two days a week, adding a third day only when needed. (Watering more than three days a week is not allowed).
Repair leaking sprinkler systems within 10 days.
Ken-Caryl Ranch Water and Sanitation District is part of a highly integrated water system and, together with Denver Water, we work tirelessly to ensure water quality from the source to your tap.

unresolved: Putting-green review stays open. No published Ranch source says which section reviews a putting green (2.05 Artificial Turf, the open-ended 2.56 Sports Courts and Facilities, or another), whether the 2.05 minimum pile of 1.75 inches applies to one, or whether a variance under Section 1.04 (Master Declaration Section 8.09) reaches that Rules standard. The page does not answer it; it tells the reader to ask the Architectural Committee in writing, and gives the Master Association's number from Section 1.06. Mark this resolved only with a written Committee answer or a new governing provision.
